_note: Accepted parity differences owned by the assets stream (docs/plan/11-WP-PORT.md 5.4). Only that stream edits this file; the lead reviews every entry. An entry: {"route": "*" or a path, "section": a section key from the report ("*" for every section), "kind": "structure|text|links|pixels|timing", "match": a regular expression, "reason": why the difference is right, "owner": "assets"}. For structure, text and links, match is tested against each differing line (without its +/- sign) and the lines it matches are dropped from the diff. For pixels it is ignored: the entry accepts the section's pixel failure. For timing it names the prototype check line (its PASS/FAIL text) that may be re-run once. Optional scopes: "width" ("390", "1440" or a list) and "mode" ("reduced", "nojs", "nowebgl", "tier0" or a list); a scoped entry applies only to comparisons at that width or in that mode. run.py refuses to start when an entry has another key, an unknown kind, a match that does not compile (or is empty, except for pixels), no reason, or an owner other than this file's stream; wp/tests/runtime-scripts-test.php checks the same.

entries.match: ^(?:vi|en)-390-t1: the world moves with no input
entries.reason: 05-DESIGN 0.6.7 notes the 390 Tier 1 ambient-motion line as timing-dependent: it measures pixel change over about 1.2 s of world time in SwiftShader, and on this machine it fails on the prototype itself (vi 0%, en 0.064% and 0.439% across runs, threshold 0.6%). The bundle and the world code are the prototype's own (one build, 11-WP-PORT.md 1.1), so a miss here is the renderer's timing, not the port; the line gets its one re-run (5.3 item 5).
